description.value: The study examined visual search performance and its gray matter correlates in Alzheimer's disease, behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia, semantic dementia, and normal controls.

spans.text: We measured visual search performance in FTLD as a way to identify mechanisms of enhanced visual function and found evidence of enhanced visual search in the SD subtype of FTLD.

value: we hypothesized that SD patients might show enhancements in visual search as compared to other dementia patients and possibly even normal controls.
we hypothesized that any paradoxical enhancements in visual search would be most apparent in conjunction search.

description.value: Tests of general cognition and functional abilities included the mini-mental state examination (MMSE) and the clinical dementia rating scale (CDR); neuropsychological tests included language, visuospatial, executive, attention, speed and working-memory measures.

spans.text: Tests of general cognition and functional abilities included the mini-mental state examination (MMSE) ( ) and the clinical dementia rating scale (CDR) ( ). Neuropsychological tests included the longest correct backward digit span ( ); a 15-item Boston naming test (BNT) ( ); measures of verbal fluency including phonemic fluency (number of D words in 1 min), category fluency (number of animals in 1 min) and design fluency (DF; number of novel designs using unique patterns of lines on the same template in 1 min); the number location condition from the visual object spatial perception (VOSP) battery ( ); a copy and 10-min recall of a simplified version of the Rey–Osterrieth; trial 1 of the design fluency subtest and Stroop (Interference condition, # correct) from the Delis–Kaplan Executive Function System ( ); and a modified Trailmaking (MT) test (time to make all correct lines) ( ).

description.value: Participants searched displays containing colored letters at display sizes of 1, 5, 15, or 30 items. The task comprised letter pop-out, color pop-out, and conjunction search blocks, with target-present and target-absent trials.

design_type.value: blocked task with randomized trials within blocks

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to look for a particular target and press the space bar when they saw it, or another key when confident that the target was absent.

stimuli.value: Colored letters displayed on a 19-inch LCD monitor; display sizes were 1, 5, 15, or 30 items, with target-present and target-absent trials.
